summary.text: Galaxy morphological classification is how astronomers divide galaxies into groups based on their visual appearance, shape, structure and distribution of light.
The most famous scheme is the Hubble sequence, devised by Edwin Hubble, which covers ellipticals, spirals, barred spirals, lenticulars and irregulars.
Gérard de Vaucouleurs extended it in 1959 to cover rings and lenses, and today classification is largely done with computational methods.

facts.label: Hubble sequence
facts.value: Devised by Edwin Hubble, later expanded

facts.label: Barred spirals
facts.value: Roughly half of all spirals have a bar

facts.label: Lenticular galaxies
facts.value: Bulge and disk, but no visible spiral structure

facts.label: De Vaucouleurs axes
facts.value: Stage, family and variety on three axes

items.prompt: A galaxy has a bright central bulge and a flat disk, but no visible spiral structure and almost no new stars forming. How is it classified?

options.label: As a spiral
As a barred spiral
As a lenticular
As an irregular

items.explain: Lenticular galaxies (S0) have a bulge and disk, but unlike spirals their disks show no spiral structure and form few stars.

items.prompt: In de Vaucouleurs's numerical stages, the lowest values go to one end of the sequence. Which galaxies sit there?

options.label: Spirals and irregulars
Ellipticals and lenticulars
Only irregulars
Only barred spirals

items.explain: Negative values of T mark early-type galaxies, meaning ellipticals and lenticulars, and positive values mark spirals and irregulars.

items.prompt: Two galaxies are compared. One keeps most of its stars in a central spheroid, the other keeps most in a disk. Which has the lower value of T?

options.label: The one with most stars in a disk
The one with most stars in a spheroid
Neither, since T has no link to stars
Both have the same T

items.explain: As a rough rule, lower T values correspond to a larger fraction of stellar mass in a spheroid or bulge relative to the disk.

items.prompt: In 1959 a galaxy specialist argued that classifying spirals only by arm tightness and the presence of a bar was not enough. What did he say was missing?

options.label: The color of the stars within the arms
The galaxy's distance from Earth in space
The mass of the central black hole
Rings and lenses, as important spiral parts

items.explain: De Vaucouleurs argued that rings and lenses are important structural components of spiral galaxies.

items.prompt: In June 2019, volunteers in a citizen science project reported something about the usual way of classifying galaxies. What was it?

options.label: It may need reassessment, especially how spiral arms relate to the nucleus
It has been proven correct in every detail
It should be dropped, because no galaxy fits it
It works only for galaxies near the Milky Way

items.explain: Galaxy Zoo citizen scientists reported that the usual Hubble classification may need reassessment, particularly for spiral arms and the galactic nucleus.

items.prompt: How is galaxy classification mostly done today?

options.label: By eye, one galaxy at a time, using Hubble's original rules
Largely with computational methods and physical morphology
By a vote among professional astronomers
Only by amateur astronomers

items.explain: Classification and morphology are now largely done using computational methods and physical morphology.
